title: Bloom filter on first key of multi-key hash joins
summary:
Hash joins with more than one equality key can now get a Bloom filter (BF) on their first key; before, they got none. Measured q09 at -18..-22% across four bench runs (best run 767.9→594.8ms). Last full bench: geomean -3.0%. Other templates moved within ±8% between runs, which is noise.

Changes:
- `src/execution/operator/join/physical_hash_join.cpp`: `CanUseBloomFilter` no longer requires `conditions.size()==1`. In `FinalizeFilters`, the BF is only considered for the filter where `join_condition[filter_idx]==0`. `PushBloomFilter` already uses condition 0's key name, type and null handling.
- `src/execution/join_hashtable.cpp`: the hash table's own hash combines all equality keys, so it doesn't match what the probe side computes for a single column. When the BF is set up and there is more than one equality key, `Finalize` now gathers key column 0 from the row locations (new static helper `InsertFirstKeyIntoBloomFilter`), hashes it alone with `VectorOperations::Hash` (the same call `BFTableFilter` uses on the probe side) and inserts that into the BF. `InsertHashes` only inserts the combined hash into the BF for single-key joins. The single-key path is unchanged.

Correctness spot-checks: a two-int-key join gave the same count with and without pushdown (pushdown blocked with `col+0` keys): 295319. A NULL-able first key with IS NOT DISTINCT FROM also matched: 196595 both ways. A VARCHAR first key and a join mixing equality and non-equality conditions both ran without errors. Bench result checks passed on all visible templates.
notes:
q04 sometimes showed +7..+15% in bench runs. I don't think the change causes it:
- q04 has only single-key joins, so the new code never runs for it.
- It stayed at +15% with the feature fully disabled (the `size()==1` gate restored).
- Run alone it came out -6.3%, and in the final full bench -2.3%.

It looks like noise that depends on run order, or code layout in `join_hashtable.cpp`, where the hot probe loops live. Moving the BF code out of `InsertHashes` into `Finalize` (the shipped version) did not change it.

Follow-up idea: build the BF on whichever equality key is most selective instead of always key 0, or push one BF per key, each with its own single-column hash.
